spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Theorem 6 treats far-left zeta-prime zeros as a weighted tail rather than merely counting them. A second comparison on selected nearby endpoints relates an even farther-left derivative tail to right-side zeta displacement, and a slowly widening logarithmic scale converts these bounds into a majority-in-a-shrinking-strip statement.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For U=T^a and a displacement delta larger than C/log T, the first assertion bounds the sum of 1/2-delta-beta' over zeta-prime zeros with beta'<1/2-delta in T<gamma'<T+U. The theorem also selects U1 and U2 between U/4 and U/2 for a comparison between a farther-left zeta-prime displacement sum and a right-side zeta displacement sum. With delta=w(T)/log T and w(T) tending to infinity, the corollary says most complex zeta-prime zeros lie to the right of the corresponding line.
directed.conceptual_reading: Weighting each exceptional zero by its excess distance makes distant failures cost more and interfaces naturally with rectangle identities. Choosing a threshold that shrinks while its logarithmic multiple grows extracts qualitative concentration from a quantitative tail estimate.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The weighted tail sum bridges zero-density input for zeta, chain-of-box contour estimates, and a statement about the proportion of zeta-prime zeros in a shrinking neighborhood of the critical line.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The theorem does not say every zeta-prime zero is near or to the right of 1/2, and a vanishing weighted tail does not by itself exclude zeros arbitrarily close to the cutoff. The second comparison uses selected endpoints rather than every interval.
directed.uncertainty: Fractions, powers, summation limits, and the exact exponent in the bound are OCR-damaged. The qualitative tail-control and shrinking-strip conclusions are prose-supported; numerical exponents and normalizations must be scan-checked.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: If one derivative has only finitely many nonreal zeros left of the critical line, the increasingly negative contribution from its real zeros forces the next logarithmic derivative to be nonzero there at large height; induction propagates the property, and the signed moment formula then becomes a one-sided RH-conditional asymptotic.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This records the article's conditional inheritance mechanism and does not establish RH or verify the partial-fraction formula independently.
related_synthesis_entries.title: RH information propagates through the derivative tower

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The key structural claim is inheritance under differentiation: once a derivative has only finitely many nonreal zeros left of the critical line, every later derivative inherits that finiteness. Under RH this converts information about the initial function into a whole derivative tower, after which the signed moment becomes effectively one-sided.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Theorem 7 states that if zeta^(m) has only finitely many nonreal zeros with real part below 1/2, then zeta^(m+j) has the same property for every j at least 1. The corollary applies this under RH to all derivatives zeta^(k), k at least 1. Theorem 8 then states an RH-conditional asymptotic for the right-of-line centered first moment of zeros of zeta^(k), involving T log log T, a logarithmic-integral term, k-dependent constants, and O(log T).
directed.conceptual_reading: Differentiation is being used as a property-propagating operation, but the preserved property is carefully limited to finiteness of a class of nonreal left-side zeros. Once the left side contributes only finitely, a signed global moment can be read as a right-side moment up to lower-order effects.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is the derivative tower together with a one-sided zero-finiteness invariant; Theorem 10's signed moment supplies the quantitative endpoint.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Inheritance does not assert that derivatives are zero-free on the left, nor does the unit prove RH. The moment formula remains conditional and does not locate individual zeros.
directed.uncertainty: The inheritance statements are clear in prose. The Theorem 8 display is heavily damaged, so its exact coefficients, summation range, and logarithmic-integral argument require scan verification.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The proof closes a global classification by combining local interlacing from Rolle's theorem with a boundary argument count. Existence of derivative zeros between consecutive trivial zeta zeros supplies a lower bound, while the argument variation supplies the matching upper count and rules out hidden nonreal zeros in the negative half-plane.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Theorem 9 states that for n at least 2, zeta-prime has a unique zero in each interval (-2n,-2n+2) and no other zeros with real part below zero. The proof counts zeta zeros in a large rectangle, obtains at least N-1 real derivative zeros by Rolle's theorem, and uses negativity of Re(zeta-prime/zeta) on the remaining boundary plus an argument change to show that exactly those N-1 zeros occur and all are real.
directed.conceptual_reading: Interlacing provides candidate zeros but not completeness. The argument principle supplies the conservation law: once the total multiplicity matches the real candidates, there is no room for additional complex zeros.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The logarithmic derivative converts zeros and poles into boundary argument variation, bridging one-dimensional real interlacing with two-dimensional complex zero classification.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Rolle's theorem alone cannot exclude nonreal zeros; the boundary sign and argument count are essential. The stated classification concerns zeta-prime in the negative half-plane and does not generalize here to all higher derivatives.
directed.uncertainty: The intervals and qualitative argument are recoverable, but the numerical argument-change sentence and rectangle notation are OCR-uncertain. Exact winding-number values should be verified against the scan.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: A reflected auxiliary function J changes the zero-location problem into an argument-variation problem on the critical line. The functional equation makes zeros of zeta-prime correspond to reflected zeros of J, while J is represented using zeta, zeta-prime, and gamma-factor logarithmic derivatives that admit Riemann-Siegel and Stirling approximations.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Within 0<Re(s)<1, the unit states that zeros of zeta-prime correspond under s to 1-s to zeros of an auxiliary J constructed from zeta, zeta-prime, and logarithmic derivatives of h(s)=pi^(-s/2)Gamma(s/2).
